annotations.text:
What actually reads as old in the current build, and what all three of these change:

- Pure black with no surface layering. Modern dark UI stacks near-blacks (#0D0D10 base, #16161C raised) so panels read as depth rather than as outlined boxes.
- Monospace for everything. Chrome is now a UI sans; monospace is kept for clipboard CONTENT, which is usually code and paths anyway.
- A 1px border around every element. Replaced by fills and spacing, with borders only where a real edge is needed.
- Every glyph tinted the accent colour. Text is now near-white; the accent is spent on the selection and one primary button.
- No radii, uppercase letterspaced labels, a function-key legend, 3-letter type codes. Replaced by radii, sentence case, key caps and real icons.

Structure is unchanged: lateral pinned pane, no sections, selected item opens in place (still optional).

SOFT — leading candidate

Layered near-black surfaces, 9-11px radii, 40px rows, real icons. The selected item becomes a raised card rather than an inverted row.

Keeps the neon green, but spends it sparingly -- selection, one badge, the primary button -- which is what lets it read modern instead of retro. This is the direction that changes the look most while keeping the app recognisably itself.

Tradeoff: the most spacing of the three, so around 9 rows visible against the current 17.

STUDIO

Professional-tool density: 32px rows, 5px radii, a column header, a real status bar. Cool neutral greys with a blue accent used only for selection and the primary action.

The closest of the three to the density you have now -- about 13 rows -- while still looking current. If Soft feels too airy, this is the one.

Tradeoff: the least distinctive. It looks like a well-made tool panel rather than like clip2.

BOLD

52px rows, 14px type, 12-16px radii, and a solid accent block for the selection. Amber rather than green, to show the palette is not load-bearing.

Reads instantly and is the easiest on the eyes at a glance.

Tradeoff: roughly 6 rows visible. For a clipboard history you hunt through, that is a real cost -- this suits someone who mostly takes one of the last few copies.

One code implication, whichever you pick.

All three style the selected row as a tinted surface with LIGHT text, rather than as inverse video. ApplyThemeId hardcodes SEL_FG to black, so a preset cannot express that today -- it needs the fifth field I raised when the themes went in, or a per-element override.

The other two are straightforward: BG stops being pure black (it is currently hardcoded too), and the chrome needs a UI sans alongside the existing monospace, so the font setting becomes two faces rather than one.
